issue.title: sase-core flake: sudo_runner fixture exec of fake sudo fails with ETXTBSY under parallel tests
issue.description:
Proposed by epic phase sase-14s.10 (sase-core "split the ten largest Rust files" epic) as
a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP; filed by the sase-14s land agent. Not caused by sase-14s: that
phase moved crates/sase_gateway/src/sudo_runner.rs into a sudo_runner/ module tree
verbatim (46 tests preserved); the fixture code is unchanged. Phase sase-14s.9 also saw
"one unrelated sudo_runner flake" pass solo on its just check rerun.

Repo: sase-core. Test (post-split path, sase-core 5154900):
crates/sase_gateway/src/sudo_runner/tests/dispatch.rs:93
`apt_get_shaped_command_uses_requested_cwd_without_sudo_chdir_option`.

Observation: failed once with ETXTBSY ("Text file busy") when the runner exec'd the
fixture's fake sudo script under a parallel `just check`; passed alone and on a full
rerun.

Likely root cause (code reading, not yet proven): `Fixture::new`
(sudo_runner/tests/support.rs:27-35, also the script writers near :468-478 and
tests/worker.rs:59-64/:109-110) writes an executable with `fs::write` and then execs it.
When another test thread forks a child (Command::spawn) while that write fd is open, the
child inherits the fd until its own exec (CLOEXEC only closes it at exec), so the
kernel refuses to exec the script with ETXTBSY. This is the classic fork/exec
text-file-busy race in multithreaded test binaries, distinct from the sudo_runner
flakes sase-15e (empty worker.pid) and sase-15f (cwd left behind).

Candidate fixes: retry the spawn on ETXTBSY in the test fixture, or serialize fixture
script writes against spawns with a shared lock. Confirm the mechanism first.

payload.entry:
RESOLVED sase-15h - sase-core sudo_runner fixture ETXTBSY flake. Fixing commits: sase-core b0a63dc3 (every fixture script is published by write-temp + chmod + atomic rename under a process-wide spawn lock; per-spawn-attempt lock inside retry_on_etxtbsy; bounded ETXTBSY-only retry of 250 x 2ms at the spawn sites as a documented backstop) plus this tale's landing repair (host-finalized in the closeout turn, no SHA cited here): the two sites that ran command.status() under the lock (handoff.rs sudo_status and spawn_internal_root_executor) now spawn under the guard and wait outside it (status_with_etxtbsy_retry; the retry helper is typed as a spawn so a wait can no longer be wrapped), the inheritance test now has a real child hold the writer descriptor after the parent closes its copy, the retry test releases the writer only after the first failed attempt (no sleeps), and the bare result.is_ok() assertions print the Err. BEFORE: parallel sase-core checks failed fleet-wide with 'Text file busy (os error 26)' on fake-sudo/worker execs; b0a63dc3 phase measured the mechanism live (foreign inheritor of a closed writer). AFTER: sudo_runner module 58 passed; synchronized spawn_lock regressions (a live sudo child does not stall another fixture publication/spawn) fail when the lock is held through the wait and pass with the fix; 60 of 60 repeated runs (12 concurrent processes x 5 rounds, 24 busy loops) passed; sase-core check 141fcdc410d4549d8645dce189f6a0ab succeeded. Every argv, cwd, environment, timeout, cancellation and ledger assertion is unchanged.

FOLLOW-UP DISPOSITIONS (lander FOLLOW-UP TRIAGE, carried into this close): (1) sase-1qt.1 note 4 wheel-cache proposal DECLINED as a cache bug: cache key 86beb74a9a2d2d03ad7707e25660b915fd68d290bdf38141e327d120e4664d50 metadata names a CLEAN core b0a63dc3 (wheel sha256 9f33941aa12e...), which predates agent_prompt_select in 45c6a260, so the missing binding is expected; the cache refuses dirty trees and rechecks source identity after build, and no incorrect exact-identity hit was shown. (2) sase-1qt.2 notes 2 and 3 are ONE drain-accounting test-order issue (cold 9 failed/3 passed, 12/12 with sase.core.git_lock_facade preloaded), retained and routed as a DISCOVERED ISSUE to active global-state epic sase-j7 (.2/.4); no duplicate task was created. (3) The import-budget proposal (sase-1qt.2 note 3, referenced by notes 4/5) is RESOLVED as this epic's own integration work: cleanup contributed +3,036 eager bytes and clan navigation +2,269 against the unchanged 12,162,484 cap; fixed by deferring the agents_sync tree, now 11,893,483 bytes (epic note #3). Phase .3 proposed no follow-up; adjacent sase-15e and sase-15f stay separately owned and untouched.

CORRECTION (2026-11-02 redo): The earlier note citing root check c3d751031ae96ebbfdca08ab1cfe32bc and core check 141fcdc410d4549d8645dce189f6a0ab describes verification on the prior tale workspace whose implementation was subsequently lost before host finalization; those runs do not prove the redo tree. Current redo evidence: linked sase-core check 4a9213fc94c163648a869096d3f07bd9 passed, and root check bfa36032ec65f99c78566f3df4a1a3a8 passed after the final lazy-import test patch corrections. No check-full was run. The spawn-only fixture guard, synchronized spawn-lock regression, deterministic child-held writer handshake, and repeatable sudo_runner evidence are recorded on reopened epic sase-1qt.
